resources.string:
To show the floating button in every app and insert your text, diktat needs Android's accessibility service. diktat is not an assistive tool for people with disabilities; the service is used only for dictation.

What the service does:
• It detects when a text field is selected in any app, so the button can appear.
• It inserts the dictated text at the cursor of that field.
• Only with the “Wave” button style does it read the brightness of a few pixels next to the button to choose black or white. The image is discarded immediately.

What it does not do: it does not read anything outside the selected text field and does not collect, store or share screen content, input or passwords. Spoken audio and text go only to the providers you set up yourself.

You can turn the service off in Android's accessibility settings at any time. If you agree, diktat opens the settings; find “diktat Floating-Button” there and switch it on.

resources.string:
Normally diktat writes down what you say. With a command word set, a dictation that begins with it becomes an instruction instead: the word is removed and the rest is sent to the AI, together with the selected text if there is any.

“Jarvis, make this more formal” rewrites the selection. “Jarvis, what is the capital of Japan” writes the answer into the field. It is the Live prompt button, reached by saying its name instead of tapping it.

The word only counts at the very start of a dictation and only as a whole word, so pick something you rarely begin a sentence with.

resources.string: Remove filler words, slips of the tongue, broken-off words and repetitions from the dictated text and add punctuation and paragraphs. Correct spelling and grammar mistakes. Keep the wording, content, tone and language and add no new information. Return only the cleaned-up text, without quotation marks or explanations.

Add only punctuation, capitalisation and paragraphs to the dictated text. Do not change, add or remove any words and do not rephrase anything. Keep the language. Return only the text, without quotation marks or explanations.

Rewrite the text as a well-structured, polite email with a suitable greeting and sign-off. Keep the core message, meaning and language, and do not invent names or facts. Return only the email, without quotation marks or explanations.

Rewrite the text as a short, casual chat message in a warm, friendly tone. Keep it brief, but keep all important information, the meaning and the language. Add nothing new. Return only the message, without quotation marks or explanations.

Write the text as a factual file note in sober, formal administrative language. Organise the content into concise bullet points and group related points. Keep all facts, names, dates and amounts unchanged and add no new information. Return only the note, without quotation marks or explanations.
